newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African oil products sales rose only 2 pct in Q2.
newsitem.headline: S.African oil products sales rose only 2 pct in Q2.

text.p: Sales of refined oil products in South Africa grew only two percent in the second quarter of 1997 to 5.16 billion litres compared to 5.06 billion litres in the same period in 1996.
The South African Petroleum Industry Association (Sapia) said in a statement that this was the second consecutive quarter in which sales growth had been slow, placing growing pressure on margins.

"This decline in growth of sales volumes will have a material adverse impact on the industry, which has been operating on fixed cents per litre marketing margins, unchanged since September 1993, despite an increase in the CPI (consumer price index) of some 35 percent since that date," Sapia said.
Sales grew by only 1.3 percent in the first quarter of the year after expanding by more than six percent in the first three quarters of 1996 and then slowing down to 4.9 percent in the last quarter.
Sapia said that gasoline sales, which accounted for more than half of total sales, increased by two percent in the second quarter to 2.66 billion litres from 2.61 billion litres.

Sales of diesel increased by 1.5 percent to 1.44 billion litres from 1.42 billion litres while jet fuel sales rose by 2.1 percent to 441 million litres from 432 million litres. Jet fuel sales had risen by 22.5 percent in the first quarter.
Sales of illuminating paraffin increased by 10.5 percent to 262 million litres from 237 million litres. Fuel oil sales fell by 4.4 percent to 173 million litres from 181 million ltres.
Bitumen sales fell 29.3 percent to 58 million litres from 82 million litres and liquefied petroleum gas sales rose 23.1 percent to 133 million litres from 108 million litres.
Sapia said the penetration of unleaded petrol as a percentage of total petrol sales had stabilised at about nine percent, which was well below the 15 to 25 percent target.
